Definition: from the same as G1174; religion:--superstition.
BiblicalUsage: The word appears once, in the hearing before Festus: the Jews have certain questions against Paul, of their own superstition, and of one Jesus, who was dead, whom Paul affirmed to be alive. Religion is the charge, and the resurrection is the answer.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the verse shows the world's verdict on the faith: they call it superstition, and we call it the resurrection.
